Which response model scores each line item

Source: R/models.R
model_map.Rd

Maps every line item of a plan to the response model that should score it, when models are fitted at a different grain from the plan – or at several. models lists the fitted models, one row each, by the line item values they cover: a channel-level model names a channel and leaves the finer columns empty; a partner-level model names the partner too.

Usage

model_map(plan, models)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

models

A data frame of fitted models: a model_id column (unique) and any of the plan's line_item_grain() columns. NA or a blank cell means the model covers any value of that column; a row with no line item columns set covers the whole plan.

Value

One row per line item, in line_item_summary()'s order: the line item columns, line_item (its key), model_id, match_level (the columns the model matched on, joined with " + "; "" for a whole-plan model, NA when unmodeled) and planned_spend.

Details

The most specific model wins. Of the models whose named values all match a line item, the one naming the most columns is chosen, so a partner-level model takes precedence over its channel's model, which is the fallback for the channel's other partners. Two matching models naming the same number of columns – a channel model and a campaign model, both covering one line – is an error naming both: which one scores it is a decision for whoever fitted them, not a guess for this function.

A line item no model covers gets model_id = NA, and a warning gives the spend left unmodeled and its share of the plan. Both the plan and the models are valid on their own; it is their pairing that leaves a gap.

See also

spend_by_model() for the spend each model scores, period by period; describe_plan(), which reports model coverage when given models.

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search", "Audio"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google", "Spotify"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40, 10)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), time = "week", name = "Q3"
)
models <- data.frame(
  model_id = c("tv", "tv_nbc", "search"),
  channel  = c("TV", "TV", "Search"),
  partner  = c(NA, "NBC", NA)
)
# NBC has its own model; ESPN falls back to TV's; Audio has none.
model_map(plan, models)
#> Warning: 1 line item(s) have no model: Audio | Spotify (10). 10 of 130 planned spend (7.7%) is unmodeled.
#>   channel partner       line_item model_id       match_level planned_spend
#> 1      TV     NBC        TV | NBC   tv_nbc channel + partner            50
#> 2  Search  Google Search | Google   search           channel            40
#> 3      TV    ESPN       TV | ESPN       tv           channel            30
#> 4   Audio Spotify Audio | Spotify     <NA>              <NA>            10
